s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive central visual impairment with color vision defects and characteristic macular changes
salient_findings: Lifelong uncorrectable visual acuity and color vision impairment in the patient
Symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally on FAF imaging
key_facts: Patient is a 21-year-old woman
Best-corrected visual acuity is 20/40 in the right eye and 20/60 in the left eye
Myopia of –6.0 diopters
Intraocular pressures are 17 mmHg bilaterally
Fundus examination shows slight enlargement of the cup-to-disc ratio in both eyes
Visual field testing reveals a central scotoma in both eyes
FAF imaging demonstrates symmetric hypoautofluorescent lesions with hyperautofluorescent borders in the central macula bilaterally
OCT shows thinning of the outer nuclear layer in the fovea, partial preservation of the ellipsoid zone, and a normal retinal nerve fiber layer
ff-ERG reveals normal scotopic responses but attenuated photopic responses and 30-Hz flicker responses with delayed implicit times in both eyes
Family history of progressive blurred central vision and color vision defects in the patient's father
Father's best-corrected visual acuity is 20/200 in both eyes
Father's intraocular pressures are 17 mmHg in the right eye and 16 mmHg in the left eye
